research_rationale: Executive Order 6322 of October 3, 1933 approves the Code of Fair Competition for the Glass Container Industry under section 3 of Title I of the National Industrial Recovery Act (NIRA); its only operative command is that approval. The text states no period, condition, 'until' date or provisional approval, and no held record cancels, suspends, supersedes or modifies the approval under section 10(b) before June 14, 1935. The approval had legal effect only through section 3 (standards of fair competition under 3(b), equity enforcement under 3(c), misdemeanor liability under 3(f)). Section 2 of S.J. Res. 113 (49 Stat. 375), approved June 14, 1935, repealed the provisions delegating power to approve or prescribe codes and providing for their enforcement, so the best supported first end of the approval's prospective operative effect is June 14, 1935. Schechter (May 27, 1935) is recorded as a validity characterization, not an end date, and June 16, 1935 is not an end. Acts and liabilities before the repeal are accrued effects.
savings_reason: Fines, injunctions, convictions, liabilities and acts done under this code before June 14, 1935 are completed effects that the repeal left in place; the section 5 antitrust exemption for action complying with the code taken before the repeal is likewise accrued, subject to the resolution's proviso, whose effect on pre-repeal action under codes the held text does not settle. Nothing in the held sources continues the approval itself after June 14, 1935.
earlier_end_check: No held record shows this code cancelled, suspended, superseded or modified under section 10(b) before June 14, 1935. I read the order's full text (signed October 3, 1933; no stated period, condition, 'until' date or provisional approval) and searched the held order texts for the code name and this order's number; the lookups report no later held order names the code or this order. The WPA list entry for this order (1933 Oct 3, p.542) records the approval only. The OFR catalog starts in 1937, so it cannot show 1933-1935 endings, and the U.S. Code and eCFR searches name this order nowhere. June 16, 1935 is not an end: section 1 of S.J. Res. 113 replaced the June 16, 1935 expiry of Title I with April 1, 1936.
scope_check: The inventory is the single operative paragraph "do order that the said code of fair competition be and is hereby approved". The preamble recitals (application, hearings, Administrator's findings under section 3(a)(1) and (2)) and the Administrator's recommendation are not separate commands. The command reaches the code only through section 3, so S.J. Res. 113 section 2 reaches all of it.
independent_command_check: The order contains no appointment, delegation, direction to an agency, report requirement, committee or other command independent of the code approval.
savings_check: Savings are the accrued effects described in the savings reason (S.J. Res. 113 and NIRA section 5 as held). The repeal's section 2 states no savings clause of its own; the held sources show no prosecution or enforcement continuing after June 14, 1935 and nothing that keeps the approval operative.

research_rationale: Executive Order 6711-A of May 15, 1934 prescribes rules for how the labor provisions of approved codes of fair competition apply to certain homeworkers and operates as a condition on previous code-approval orders. The order's own duration clause says it remains in effect 'until revoked or modified by my further order or by order of the Administrator for Industrial Recovery'; that is a continuing term with no date, and no held record shows a revocation or modification before June 14, 1935. Section 2 of S.J. Res. 113, approved June 14, 1935, repealed the provisions delegating power to approve or prescribe codes and providing for their enforcement, which removed the approved codes these rules operate on; the best supported first end is June 14, 1935. Schechter (May 27, 1935) is a validity characterization, not an end date, and June 16, 1935 is not an end.
savings_reason: Homework certificates issued, and acts done in reliance on the rules, before June 14, 1935 are completed effects that the repeal left in place; the section 5 antitrust exemption for pre-repeal action under codes is accrued, subject to the resolution's proviso whose effect the held text does not settle.
